title: NEVER A DULL MOMENT: DISTRIBUTIONAL PROPERTIES AS A BASELINE FOR TIME-SERIES CLASSIFICATION
summary: The paper asks whether extremely simple distributional features can provide a strong baseline for time-series classification, in contrast to complex dynamical or deep models. It fits a linear SVM on two features that ignore temporal ordering, the mean and standard deviation (FTM), and compares it with catch22 + FTM across the 128 UEA/UCR problems and a schizophrenia rs-fMRI case study. FTM beats chance on 69 of 128 problems, reaches 100% accuracy on GunPointOldVersusYoung and InsectEPGRegularTrain, and achieves 67.5% balanced accuracy on the neuroimaging task versus 63.6% for catch22 + FTM.

match_target.why: This is the user's hinted result and the cheapest direct demonstration of the paper's central claim: two distributional features plus a linear SVM perfectly separate a UCR class, using a small dataset and no catch22 or neuroimaging pipeline.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: bounded accuracy on a small UEA/UCR test split (<2,000 examples); the paper gives no numeric SD for this 100% value, so use the fixed 2.0 absolute-point band (98-100%).

requirements.stmt: Compute only two FTM features: the mean and standard deviation.
requirements.quote: we computed the FTM feature set containing two features: the mean (μ) and standard deviation (σ).

requirements.stmt: Do not z-normalize individual time series before FTM extraction; preserve raw measurement scale.
requirements.quote: If all time series were individually z-score transformed, there would be no class differences in mean or standard deviation for any problem
A linear SVM was fit on the train set and used to generate predictions for the test set.

requirements.stmt: Z-score features using train-set mean and standard deviation, then apply the same scaling to test data.
requirements.quote: features were normalized as a z-score by computing the mean and standard deviation of each feature in the train set

requirements.stmt: Generate 30 train-test resamples: the designated split plus 29 seeded resamples preserving class proportions.
requirements.quote: we generated 29 additional (seeded) resamples of the data that preserve the class proportions of the designated split

requirements.stmt: Use classification accuracy as the UEA/UCR performance metric.
requirements.quote: Classification accuracy was used as the performance metric, following prior work.

requirements.stmt: Test chance performance with a p-value from the distribution of 30 resampled FTM accuracies.
requirements.quote: we calculated a p-value of the chance probability against the distribution of 30 resampled FTM accuracy values for each problem.

requirements.stmt: For the comparison model, use the catch22 set of 22 time-series features plus FTM.
requirements.quote: we used the catch22 set of 22 time-series features [17]

requirements.stmt: Exclude problems with fewer than 10 real values before all-or-mostly-missing values from catch22 comparisons.
requirements.quote: due to presence of time series that had < 10 real values before containing all or mostly missing values

requirements.stmt: For the case study, evaluate balanced accuracy with 10-fold cross-validation and 10 repeats.
requirements.quote: Model performance was evaluated as balanced accuracy using 10-fold cross-validation (CV) with 10 repeats

requirements.stmt: For the case-study SVM, set C = 1, disable shrinking, and use balanced class weights.
requirements.quote: setting the regularization parameter C = 1, disabling the shrinking heuristic, and using balanced class weights.

requirements.stmt: Use 82 brain regions: 68 cortical and 14 subcortical regions per participant.
requirements.quote: extracted for each of 68 cortical [22] and 14 subcortical [23] regions per participant.

requirements.stmt: The FTM case-study model has 164 SVM input features (2 x 82).
requirements.quote: the FTM-only model had a total of 2 × 82 = 164 SVM input features

requirements.stmt: The catch22 + FTM case-study model has 1968 SVM input features (24 x 82).
requirements.quote: the FTM + catch22 model had a total of 24 × 82 = 1968 features.

requirements.stmt: Use a corrected resampled t-test for comparing FTM and catch22 + FTM.
requirements.quote: we implemented a correlated test statistic [18] that corrects the traditional T-statistic to account for the violation of the assumption of independence

data.name: GunPointOldVersusYoung
